nodes_removed: Members and bookmarks enter the kernel (0.15.0)

nodes_removed.doc: Kernel ceremony ruling: a knowledge base gains the vocabulary to mount another knowledge base and to cite a citizen that lives there. [Member] pins a mounted knowledge base to an edition (its committed backup's identity hash and event-log sequence) with a read or write intent; [Bookmark] names a citizen in a member (its knowledge base, label, name, and the edition it was resolved against) with exactly one IN_MEMBER edge to that member. Both are Provenance-rooted machinery, bracketed because a designer never authors either as subject matter; where a member lives on disk is settings, never canon, and a knowledge base's own citizens point at a bookmark through their own relation vocabulary. Any knowledge base holding member entries plays the world role — a role, never a type; init --world seeds the same knowledge base plus the member settings block, and the first gated round mounts the members. The delta gate checks their shape; resolution against the member's backup, the stale-pin advisory, and the drift query are the next rung. Additive; kernel 0.14.0 -> 0.15.0, delivered to existing knowledge bases by kernel-migrate.
